articles.title: Save $900 Off the Asus ROG Flow Z13 Gaming Laptop, More Powerful and Versatile Than the Xbox Ally X20
articles.summary: For this week only, Best Buy is offering a major price drop on a compact convertible laptop that doubles as a gaming powerhouse. The diminutive Asus ROG Flow Z13 gaming laptop with 64GB of RAM is now available for just $2,099.99 with free shipping after a massive $900 off discount.
body: The Asus ROG Flow Z13 is a 13.4" 2-in-1 convertible laptop that weighs in at only 2.65 pounds in tablet mode. That's about one pound heavier than the Xbox Ally X handheld, which weighs in at 1.6 pounds. A premium laptop deserves premium build quality, and the Flow Z13 doesn't disappoint with a blacked out CNC aluminum alloy chassis and Corning Gorilla Glass Victus screen protection. The keyboard can be detached so that the Z13 can be used as a tablet.

This particular configuration is equipped with a 13.4" 2560x1600 180Hz IPS display, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 CPU with AMD Radeon 8060S iGPU, 64GB of LPDDR5X-8000Mhz RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The Radeon 8060S is a technological marvel of an iGPU. It's far and away the most powerful integrated graphics solution on the market and nearly the same gaming performance as a discrete RTX 5060 mobile (faster than an RTX 4060 mobile). It's considerably more powerful than the Ryzen Z2 Extreme APU found in the highest-end handheld gaming PCs like the ROG Xbox Ally X or Legion Go 2.
points: For this week only, Best Buy is offering a major price drop on a compact convertible laptop that doubles as a gaming powerhouse.

articles.title: Point Break TV Show Gets the Green Light at AMC
articles.summary: AMC has given its Point Break TV show the green light. A sequel series based on Keanu Reeves and Patrick Swayze's iconic action movie has officially received a series order from AMC and AMC+, according to Variety.
body: "More than three decades after the events of the original Point Break film, a new heist crew inspired by the Ex-Presidents has emerged and the FBI must rely on a mysterious ex-pro surfer with a checkered past to infiltrate them," an official logline shared by the site said.

Butterfly producer Dave Kalstein and Sugar producer Christopher C. Rogers will lead the new Point Break show as co-showrunners and executive producers. Alcon's Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson are executive producers, with Ben Roberts and Julia Cohen also in the mix.

Being set 30 years after the events of the original film, it's unclear if Reeves will play any part in the series. Additional plot information, including who will star in the project, has also not been revealed.

Point Break is a quintessential '90s movie. Originally released back in July 1991, the Kathryn Bigelow-directed film starred Reeves as FBI agent Johnny Utah and Swayze as a bank robber/surfer named Bodhi.

articles.title: GTA 6 Developer Is Fighting Drones And Hackers To Keep The Game’s Secrets Safe
articles.summary: As the studio behind one of the most highly anticipated games of all time, GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games has divulged more details on how it keeps its secrets. As part of a hearing, which began yesterday at the Glasgow Employment Tribunal--in which Rockstar Games has been accused of unlawfully…
body: "Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula," Rockstar said in its opening note (via IGN ). "The standards and expectations regarding information security and privacy are exponentially beyond that of most employers."

The company claims that people are so hell-bent on peeking behind the curtain that it was forced to coat its building windows with a privacy film after aerial drones were used to spy on employees and photograph the inside of the building. Because of that, Rockstar has had to implement numerous security measures, such as enforcing strict no-photography rules for visitors, banning external storage devices on office premises, and restricting remote work for employees. The developer also has a full-time team of five investigators and a director who keep an eye out for potential leaks.
points: As the studio behind one of the most highly anticipated games of all time, GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games has divulged more details on how it keeps its secrets.

articles.title: Save $10 Off the PlayStation 5 Disc Drive and Turn Your PS5 Digital Edition Console Into a 4K Blu-ray Player
articles.summary: Did you get a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition console and wish you had purchased the disc edition so that you can watch 4K Blu-ray movies on it? That's an easy fix. Walmart currently has limited stock of the official PlayStation 5 Disc Drive for $79 with free shipping.
body: The PlayStation 5 disc drive is compatible with the PS5 Slim Edition console only, not the original bulkier model. It attaches neatly onto your PS5 Slim digital edition console without any tools required. You essentially pop off the original cover and snap the drive into place. You will, however, need an active internet connection to set it up.

The disc drive allows you to play PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 4 games on physical disc media just like the disc edition console. Keep in mind, however, that starting January 2028, newly released PlayStation games will be exclusively digital, so going forward this won't be as big of a perk as it used to be. Also, it's important to note that some "physical" copies of games are simply voucher codes in physical boxes. For example, although Grand Theft Auto V included a physical disc, the upcoming Grand Theft Auto VI game will be a code in a box.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering’s Newest Legendary Artifact Destroys Whole Universes (and Your Creatures)
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s next set is the world-bending Reality Fracture, which centers around an alternate universe with twisted mirror versions of many the game’s characters (available for preorder at Amazon ).
body: The first card is a key object in Reality Fracture: The Echoverse Fulcrum. This Mythic Rare legendary artifact is meant to merge universes together, but its functional effect is a board wipe with a little bit of card selection attached.

Colorless cards have had plenty of conditional board wipes like this before, but to my eyes, the low initial mana cost and immediate benefit of drawing and then discarding a card could make this one more broadly useful in a format like Commander. Five mana to activate its ability and only at sorcery speed are both real drawbacks, but that’s easier to stomach when you’ve already gotten something (admittedly minor) out of it.

The other card we are revealing depicts the final moments of Reality Fracture’s hero-turned-villain, Jace. Vraska’s Final Mercy is a Rare sorcery that can either be a removal spell or effectively draw you two cards as it either strikes down or builds up Jace himself.

articles.title: EA’s New Owners May Be Considering An Even Bigger Gaming Empire
articles.summary: EA has officially been sold, and with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund now the majority shareholder in the video game company, talks are reportedly underway to merge it with Savvy Games Group, the gaming and esports holding company that's also owned by the PIF.
body: Speaking to Bloomberg, sources said the PIF is aiming to foster "better coordination" between its gaming assets, and the merger could happen once it completes its plan to acquire Chinese mobile gaming company Moonton, a deal valued at $6 billion. The PIF also owns Pokemon Go developer Scopely and game publisher SNK, and it holds sizable stakes in video game publishers like Nintendo, Capcom, and Koei Tecmo.

The move could face scrutiny from regulators across the globe, however, as this would place several of the biggest gaming franchises in the world under one roof, including EA Sports FC, Battlefield, and mobile juggernauts like Monopoly Go. While EA's acquisition is valued at $55 billion, the massive leveraged buyout has also saddled the game company with billions of debt that needs to be addressed.

The PIF is the majority owner of EA Games, with a 93.4% stake in the company, while its partners Silver Lake and Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner's private equity firm, Affinity Partners, own 5.5% and 1.1% of the company, respectively.

articles.title: Silksong's New Replacement Is About to Become the Best Action Game of the Year
articles.summary: What to do when you're a writer incapable of finishing a story? Simple: you kidnap an editor. Optionally, you may use your vampire powers to trap said editor inside your manuscript and have him fight demonic creatures until he's cleared up your work.
body: In Chronoscript: The Endless End, an exploration-based action-adventure game developed by DeskWorks, you take on the role of Frederick G. Muller, a famous editor who just received a new assignment. All seems well until the job leads him to a creepy, remote mansion, where the resident vampire lady, Viola S. Chambers, teleports him into her unfinished story. As an immortal being (vampire perk), Viola has been working on her story for literal ages, clearly unable to wrap it up without editorial assistance. Poor Frederick is forced to walk his way through Viola's manuscript in the most literal sense — let us hope he's paid by the hour.

Upon seeing Chronoscript: The Endless End for the first time, I was deeply in awe of its visual style. The moody darkness, the hand-drawn charm (yes, everything's hand-drawn), and the abundance of detail in the 2D illustrations create a unique, inky look. On top of that, Chronoscript: The Endless End uses a variety of 3D elements. As you steer a 2D Frederick through the 2D Metroidvania-style chambers, you'll see 3D pens, ink bottles, and feathers on the side of your screen. Zoom out, and you see a 3D Viola hunched over her unfinished draft.
points: What to do when you're a writer incapable of finishing a story?

articles.title: One of Nintendo's Greatest '80s Games Is Still the Perfect Weekend Obsession
articles.summary: When people talk about Zelda, they rarely mention Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link. It’s the black sheep of the franchise, often regarded as only slightly better than the disastrous Philips CD-i entries. It also happens to be the perfect weekend obsession in the weeks leading up to the Nov.
body: When Nintendo first launched Zelda 2 on Dec. 1, 1988, retailers found themselves apologizing to eager consumers for running out of copies to sell. By the following year, demand had finally settled enough that my mother took my birthday money to town and came back with the game. Thrilled, I let my sister play first as I pored over the instruction manual, savoring every detail. I quickly realized it didn’t look much like its predecessor at all. Change isn’t always bad, but my early exposure made me conclude that in this case, it was.

Over the years, I’ve come to love Zelda 2, enough that I now consider it one of the best games ever made, even though it was highly unpredictable. I’ve played through it numerous times, usually over the course of a few days or a lazy weekend, which is why I know it’s the ideal old game to turn to when you’re looking for a stroll down memory lane that won’t end in just a couple of hours.

articles.title: Switch 2 Update Secretly Makes Digital Game Sharing Much Better
articles.summary: Everyone is focused on VRR (variable refresh rate) support for Switch 2 while docked. But the latest system update just provided a notable quality-of-life improvement for people--especially families--who own multiple Switch 2 and Switch consoles.
body: For example, say your child is playing Super Mario Bros. Wonder on your old Switch OLED, but you want to play it on your Switch 2. You both can actually play the title simultaneously by turning off Wi-Fi on the original hybrid console. Then, on your Switch 2, you can utilize an online license to jump around as the mustached plumber, too. We tested this out successfully.

This also helps a lot between manually sending virtual game cards back and forth between Switch and Switch 2 systems. Now I can just start say, Blasphemous, on either system without having to actually send it from the previous place to a new one. Sure, it's not as smooth as using apps across Apple devices, but it's a step in the right direction.

Here's Nintendo's official language for the version 23.0.0 update, which incorporates Switch 2 and Switch. "When starting software, if a virtual game card cannot be ejected from another console because it is powered off or otherwise not connected to the internet, there will be a prompt to start the software using an online license."
points: Everyone is focused on VRR (variable refresh rate) support for Switch 2 while docked.

articles.title: Death Stranding Franchise Likely Barely Broke Even, Could Explain Sony Dropping Physint – Analyst
articles.summary: With Sony no longer involved in the production of Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor, Physint, people are wondering why the PlayStation company decided to part ways with the veteran game designer's upcoming game.
body: Why would it take another loss in the court of public opinion? Reportedly, Kojima's recent games haven't been big earners for Sony, which could be why Sony decided to cease funding for Physint.

According to a Bloomberg report, people familiar with the project have expressed concerns about Physint's development, as it has reportedly missed deadlines and could be going over budget. With Physint potentially being a timed exclusive for PlayStation, it's claimed that the company was reluctant to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in a game it would not own.

Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliott also weighed in on the situation, saying, "From a strictly financial perspective, though, I can understand Sony's position. In a vacuum, anyway. PR and optics still matter. Ballpark math: word on the street is that the first Death Stranding cost about $100 million to make, and the second somewhere in the $150 million – $200 million ballpark (longer dev cycle, COVID, and all that). Depending on marketing overhead and the opportunity cost of pulling those Guerrilla developers onto Death Stranding, the franchise has almost certainly broken even--but not by much."

articles.title: After Sony tells fans they don't own digital games, one Consumer Rights group is tracking all the times PlayStation said the opposite
articles.summary: Last month, Sony argued that "reasonable consumers" already know they don't really own the digital goods they paid for. The Consumer Rights wiki has now made a list collecting more than 30 examples where Sony told customers they do, in fact, own the digital games they paid for.
body: A class action lawsuit recently filed against Sony alleged the PlayStation Store isn't clear enough about the fact that digital purchases don't equal digital ownership. Once a player makes a purchase on the PlayStation Store, they're paying for a digital license that's revocable at any point in time - the purchase doesn't guarantee you'll have access to a particular game or DLC or cosmetic pack forever.
One of the more recent examples can be found in Marvel's Wolverine's FAQ section: "Standard Edition owners can also upgrade to the Digital Deluxe Edition content."

The lawsuit claimants said Sony was in breach of a California Law that made it "unlawful for a seller of a digital good to advertise or offer for sale a digital good to a purchaser with the terms 'buy,' 'purchase,' or any other term which a reasonable person would understand to confer an unrestricted ownership interest in the digital good." (Reasonability doesn't seem like something you could measure in court, but I digress.) A digital vendor can get around the law by giving customers clear information about the licenses they're paying for. We'll see how the suit plays out over the coming weeks and months.
points: Last month, Sony argued that "reasonable consumers" already know they don't really own the digital goods they paid for.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation director says Square Enix would have to compromise "the quality of the final chapter" to ship the game fully on disc
articles.summary: Physical versions of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation require a download anyway because Square Enix would've had to compromise the game in some fashion to contain the entire mammoth adventure in a disc. At least, that's the reasoning series director Naoki Hamaguchi has given.
body: Anyone sitting in the venn diagram middle of Final Fantasy 7 fan and physical games collector might have gone from extremely happy to kinda bummed earlier this week. The third and final part of the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy is shipping in a physical format on all three major consoles (hurray), but you'll still need to download additional game data to get going.

"Each platform has limitations when it comes to physical media capacity, but we believed that compromising the quality of the final chapter in order to achieve a fully on-disc release would ultimately not be in the best interest of many fans," said Remake trilogy director Naoki Hamaguchi in an online statement.

"We understand that this decision may not meet everyone's expectations. Even so, in today's market, where the industry is steadily moving toward a disc-less future, we believe there is real value in being able to offer a physical edition at all," he added.

articles.title: Modder adds 235 destructible Flock cameras to GTA 5 so you can 'do whatever the flock you want' to them
articles.summary: You've no doubt spent dozens of hours in GTA 5 doing millions of dollars of property damage with your fleet of speeding vehicles and arsenal of deadly weapons. But what if you could do something good for the city of Los Santos while still satisfying your insatiable bloodlust and appetite for…
body: Thanks to the GTALPR mod (which stands for Grand Theft Automated License Plate Reader), you can! The mod adds 235 Flock cameras to GTA 5, and in the modder's words, you can "do whatever the flock you want" to 'em. Shoot 'em. Smash 'em. Take 'em out with cars and tanks and shotguns. And you can even make a tidy profit while fighting back against the surveillance state.

What's especially cool about GTALPR, created by modder Morry, is that these cameras aren't just static props, they actually work. They'll photograph you as you drive past them, and you can save and format these photos for social media or your own scrapbook. The cameras will also alert the cops to your location, sometimes even if you're not breaking any laws—just like real Flock cameras are prone to do, because they suck.
